document_check.note: Whitfield T, Chouliaras L, Morrell R, et al. The criteria used to rule out mild cognitive impairment impact dementia incidence rates in subjective cognitive decline. Alzheimer's Res Ther 2024;16:142. Essex Memory Clinic routine data; SCD-Winblad n = 86, SCD-Jak/Bondi n = 185; dementia incidence 14.9 v 75.5 per 1,000 person-years; age-adjusted IRR 3.7 (1.5 to 9.3).

cited_result: Dementia incidence in SCD samples defined by excluding MCI with Winblad criteria (5/86; 14.9 per 1,000 person-years) versus Jak/Bondi criteria (52/185; 75.5 per 1,000 person-years); age-adjusted incidence rate ratio 3.7 (1.5 to 9.3).
tool_reason: The cited result is an incidence estimate (dementia incidence rates under two MCI-exclusion definitions), which the brief assigns to the JBI checklist for prevalence (and incidence) studies.

domains.domain: Item 1: Sample frame appropriate to address the target population
domains.rationale: A memory-clinic database of patients presenting with cognitive symptoms suits memory-clinic SCD patients.

signalling.question: Was the sample frame appropriate to address the target population?
signalling.quote: This study utilized routine healthcare data collected by the Essex Memory Clinic, a service operated by Essex Partnership University National Health Service Foundation Trust. The clinic provides in-depth assessment for patients presenting with cognitive symptoms.

domains.rationale: All eligible database patients were used, but eligibility required a follow-up visit at least 12 months later, which conditions on return to clinic. Patients whose self-reported decline could not be confirmed from case notes were excluded. The number lost through these requirements is not reported in the text.

signalling.question: Were study participants sampled in an appropriate way?
signalling.quote: both samples only included patients aged ≥ 55 years at their initial assessment, with at least one follow-up visit ≥ 12 months later.

signalling.question: Were exclusions after sampling appropriate?
signalling.quote: For these individuals, a case note review was undertaken; where self-reported difficulties could not be confirmed, patients were not eligible for reclassification as SCDJak/Bondi.

domains.rationale: Five events in the Winblad sample give a sevenfold-wide confidence interval for the incidence rate. The authors also acknowledge a lack of power for a finer three-group comparison.

signalling.question: Was the sample size adequate?
signalling.quote: The incidence rate [95% CI] of dementia was 14.9 [4.9 to 34.9] per 1,000 person-years.

signalling.question: Was power acknowledged as limited?
signalling.quote: Unfortunately, this study lacked statistical power to investigate this empirically.

domains.domain: Item 4: Subjects and setting described in detail
domains.rationale: Demographic, cognitive and follow-up characteristics by sample are reported in Table 2, and the setting is described.

signalling.question: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
signalling.quote: There were no significant between-sample differences for sex, years of education, ethnicity, nor year of first visit. However, the median [interquartile range; IQR] age (years) of the SCDJak/Bondi sample (74.4 [66.5 to 80.1]) was greater than that of the SCDWinblad sample (70.0 [61.7 to 74.8]; p < 0.01).

domains.domain: Item 5: Data analysis with sufficient coverage of the identified sample
domains.rationale: Missingness was at most 5% for all variables in both samples. Missing cognitive scores were coded as impaired, which affects classification rather than coverage.

signalling.question: Was the data analysis conducted with sufficient coverage of the identified sample?
signalling.quote: For both samples, missingness was ≤ 5% for all variables.

signalling.question: How were missing classification data handled?
signalling.quote: Missing values in these six measures (including discontinued TMT trials) were coded as impaired, because missingness was associated with poorer CAMCOG-R scores

domains.domain: Item 6: Valid methods for identification of the condition
domains.rationale: Dementia was diagnosed by multidisciplinary consensus using ICD-10 and dedicated subtype criteria. The SCD definitions follow published SCD, Winblad and Jak/Bondi criteria, although Winblad was applied without a rigid cut-off.

signalling.question: Were valid methods used for the identification of the condition (incident dementia)?
signalling.quote: At present, dementia diagnosis is made according to the International Classification of Diseases (tenth revision) [30] in conjunction with dedicated criteria, including AD [31], vascular dementia (VaD) [32], dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) [33] and frontotemporal dementia (FTD) [34].

signalling.question: Was the diagnosis made by consensus?
signalling.quote: The diagnosis of dementia (including subtype) was made by consensus, which improves diagnostic accuracy compared to individual clinicians [51].

domains.domain: Item 7: Condition measured in a standard, reliable way for all participants
domains.rationale: How dementia was ascertained differed systematically between the compared samples. 111 of the 185 SCD-Jak/Bondi patients carried a clinic MCI diagnosis and were recalled at 1 year, whereas SCD-Winblad patients (all SCI) were recalled at 2 years, and visit counts differed. Diagnostic criteria changed over the 24-year period, and follow-up diagnoses were made in routine care with no blinding to the baseline label reported.

signalling.question: Was the condition measured in a standard way for all participants (follow-up schedule)?
signalling.quote: Patients who receive a diagnosis of MCI or SCI are invited for reassessment at 1 or 2 years, respectively.

signalling.question: How many of the compared sample carried the clinic MCI label?
signalling.quote: The SCDJak/Bondi sample included the remaining 74 patients from the SCDWinblad sample, as well as 111 patients originally diagnosed with MCIWinblad.

signalling.question: Did ascertainment intensity differ between samples?
signalling.quote: Whilst the median [IQR] number of visits was greater in the SCDJak/Bondi versus SCDWinblad sample (3 [2 to 5], versus 3 [2 to 4]; p = 0.02), the length of follow-up (years) did not differ

signalling.question: Were diagnostic criteria constant over time?
signalling.quote: The criteria used to diagnose dementia varied over the data collection period, as criteria were superseded by updated versions.

signalling.question: Were follow-up diagnoses made blind to the baseline diagnosis?
signalling.quote: Searched for 'blind', 'aware' and any statement on masking of follow-up assessors to the baseline SCI or MCI label; none found.

domains.rationale: Incidence rates per person-year with CIs and a Mantel-Haenszel age-adjusted IRR are appropriate. The 74 patients shared between samples are treated as independent (which is conservative), and deaths are not mentioned.

signalling.question: Was there appropriate statistical analysis?
signalling.quote: The incidence rate of dementia was calculated for each sample by dividing the number of incident dementia cases by the total person-years at risk, and multiplying by 1,000.

signalling.question: Was confounding by age handled?
signalling.quote: If between-sample differences were observed for any initial characteristic(s) (other than cognitive measures), this was treated as confounding and a Mantel-Haenszel adjusted incidence rate ratio was also calculated.

domains.domain: Item 9: Response rate adequate, or low response managed appropriately
domains.rationale: For routine records, the analogue of non-response is failure to return for follow-up. The text gives neither the number of otherwise-eligible SCD patients excluded for lacking a 12-month follow-up nor a comparison of excluded and included patients (the flowchart is not in the extracted text).

signalling.question: Was the response (follow-up) rate adequate, and if not, was it managed appropriately?
signalling.quote: Searched for counts of patients without a follow-up visit, loss to follow-up, deaths, and comparisons of excluded with included patients; the text refers only to "See Fig. 1 for a flowchart outlining the derivation of the SCDWinblad (n = 86) and SCDJak/Bondi (n = 185) samples."

overall: High (review rule for the JBI prevalence checklist: item 7, standard and reliable measurement of the condition, is 'No')
overall_rationale: The cited incidence divergence depends on how dementia was ascertained in the two samples, and ascertainment differed systematically between them. Recall intervals depended on the baseline clinic label, which maps onto the compared samples; visit counts differed; criteria changed over time; and no blinding is reported. Imprecision (5 events in one sample) and conditioning on a 12-month follow-up visit add further concerns.
